### enums — original scope contract

**Scope source:** `analyses/enums/scope.json`. **Coverage source:** `analyses/enums/value-coverage.json`; global closure source is `synthesis/value-coverage.json`.
**All original contract fields:**
- **topic:** enums
- **owner:** EnumAstra
- **mode:** DOCS ONLY
- **source:**
  - **assigned_title:** Why can't we agree on what an enum is?
  - **current_title:** Why do we keep reinventing enums?
  - **source_id:** JaOzpMQEUnI
  - **source_identity:** youtube:JaOzpMQEUnI
  - **url:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JaOzpMQEUnI
  - **channel:** rats159
  - **published:** 2026-09-11
  - **duration_seconds:** 571
  - **capture_owner:** SharedVideoCapture
  - **coverage:** Full 108-line creator transcript; supplied audience strata; four inspected 3x3 storyboard sheets. Exact miniature screen punctuation remains limited.
- **subject:** Enum and union semantic models, callable naming analogy, finite case APIs, boundary validity, layout, evolution and broadly useful serialization.
- **workloads:**
  - Protocol state and integer wire codes
  - Text-or-number parse result
  - Two same-payload business alternatives
  - Generic recursive expression tree
  - Finite options and permission sets
  - Library evolution with unknown wire values
  - Named callback and capturing anonymous callback
- **outcome:** Evidence-backed independent proposal with one canonical mechanism or precise reasons for distinctions; no ratification or implementation.
- **finite_peer_corpus:**
  - **item 1:**
    - **peer:** C
    - **version_target:** C23; C11 N1570 historical contrast
    - **reason:** Required implicit integer and untagged-union contrast.
  - **item 2:**
    - **peer:** C++
    - **version_target:** C++23
    - **ecosystem:**
      - std::variant
      - Glaze enum/variant JSON
    - **reason:** Required baseline; scoped enum, library sum and strong ordinary serialization comparator.
  - **item 3:**
    - **peer:** Rust
    - **version_target:** Stable official release/reference pinned by capture
    - **ecosystem:**
      - Serde enum representations
    - **reason:** Required baseline; nominal labeled sums, niches, exhaustive matching and closure identity.
  - **item 4:**
    - **peer:** Odin
    - **version_target:** Current official documentation/commit pinned by capture
    - **reason:** Explicit owner question; enum, union, bit_set and integer-cast contrast.
  - **item 5:**
    - **peer:** Zig
    - **version_target:** 0.15.2 official reference
    - **reason:** Tagged versus bare union, non-exhaustive numeric enum and introspection contrast.
  - **item 6:**
    - **peer:** Swift
    - **version_target:** 6.2 or precise captured language-guide version
    - **reason:** Raw/associated/indirect enums, enum protocols and library evolution.
  - **item 7:**
    - **peer:** TypeScript
    - **version_target:** 5.9; precise live handbook revision recorded separately
    - **reason:** Video peer and structural labeled sums versus runtime enum objects.
  - **item 8:**
    - **peer:** Python
    - **version_target:** 3.14 official docs
    - **reason:** Required baseline; rich Enum/Flag/IntEnum boundary and reflection APIs.
  - **item 9:**
    - **peer:** Go
    - **version_target:** 1.26 official spec
    - **reason:** Required baseline and video peer; typed constants without enum closure.
  - **item 10:**
    - **peer:** Java
    - **version_target:** 25 official specification/API
    - **reason:** Required baseline; enum objects, sealed sums and target-typed lambdas.
  - **item 11:**
    - **peer:** .NET/C#
    - **version_target:** .NET 10/C# 14 official specification/API
    - **reason:** Required baseline; numeric enum validity, flags, reflection and delegate callbacks.
- **owner_questions:**
  - Which enum features, ideas, representations, operations and APIs serve ordinary workloads?
  - Should enum and union values have implicit conversions, an explicit relationship, or no relationship?
  - Does enum/union parallel named function/anonymous lambda, and should naming be their only difference?
  - What are the separate roles of nominal identity, structural identity, labels and payload-type identity?
  - How do payloads, repeated payload types, generics, recursion, exhaustiveness, empty and singleton types behave?
  - How should constructors, matching, narrowing, methods and traits compose?
  - What layout, niche, FFI and wire discriminant controls are safe and useful?
  - How do C implicit integer conversions compare with Odin rejection, checked casts, arithmetic and invalid values?
  - How do flags/sets, introspection, iteration and serialization fit one mechanism?
  - What remains closed, what can evolve and where do open alternatives belong?
  - Which alternatives best serve beginner and expert on the same programs?
  - What is current Jet code versus ratified law, and what exact proof remains?
  - Which performance hypotheses need matched measurements rather than assertion?
- **capability_dimensions:**
  - identity
  - labels
  - payloads
  - repeated_payloads
  - generics_recursion
  - empty_singleton
  - exhaustiveness_narrowing
  - constructors
  - methods_traits
  - representation_niches
  - ffi_wire
  - integer_validity_arithmetic
  - flags_sets
  - introspection_iteration_serialization
  - evolution_open_closed
  - function_lambda_identity_capture
- **evidence_lanes:**
  - **primary_video:** Shared capture; analyst reads full transcript.
  - **audience:** Representative strata plus corrections; missing roots explicitly limited.
  - **primary_peer_sources:** Two independent Luna max scout slices; analyst reads captures and owns reasoning.
  - **jet:** Shared navigation and precise missing evidence requests only.
  - **runtime:** Three authored focused inputs; seven Main execution/check receipts inspected and embedded in probes.json. Exact dirty binary hash retained; not a current-tree or complete all-tier proof.
  - **performance:** Hypotheses only unless matched receipts supplied.
- **known_limits:**
  - Current video title differs from assigned playlist title.
  - Comment export has missing parent roots; it cannot establish complete audience coverage.
  - Living references will be labeled by captured date/version; version ambiguity is not silently resolved.
  - Source reading is not runtime proof.
  - New syntax and APIs remain proposed; full ballot reader receipts are Main's responsibility.
- **exclusions:**
  - Implementation edits
  - Tower writes
  - Broad repository rescans
  - Video recapture
  - Specialist niche enum libraries
  - Claims of universal superiority
  - Unmatched performance claims
- **publication_owner:** Main
**Denominator reading rule:** selected finite corpus only; this contract does not authorize implementation, runtime, performance or ratification beyond its recorded evidence.

  - **source_identity:** youtube:nzjy0EFrzbk
  - **physical_kind:** video
  - **channel:** xyve (@xyve7)

  - **duration_seconds:** 95

  - **identity_evidence:** target-mine-playlist-20260911/sources/nzjy0EFrzbk.info.json
- **subject_boundary:** Every stable standard-library Rust iterator capability at the officially verified current stable release, its stock-Jet semantic correspondence, and a finite set of broadly useful ecosystem enhancements. Names alone do not establish semantic parity.
- **workloads:**
  - Single-pass lazy filter/map/collect on owned and borrowed collections
  - Mutable iteration, overlapping read windows, and disjoint mutable chunks without aliasing
  - Fallible parsing and early exit with visible remaining input
  - Bidirectional and exact-size traversal, including empty/infinite/overflow boundaries
  - Ordinary grouping, joins, deduplication, windows and top-k data processing
  - Ordered and unordered parallel reductions and bounded asynchronous streams
  - File/text/OS collection producers and deterministic resource cleanup
- **outcome:** Independent evidence-backed parity census and proposal for stock Jet to match stable Rust and exceed the best broadly useful peer mechanisms without overlapping Jet iteration semantics. No implementation or ratification.
- **owner_questions:**
  - Does stock Jet cover ALL stable Rust std iterator functionality at a pinned current release?
  - Which precise stable capabilities are equivalent, partial, missing, or unknown, including conversion and collection relationships?
  - Which nightly, itertools, Rayon and async-stream capabilities belong in a coherent stock Jet design?
  - What Rust strengths should Jet adopt, what friction should it avoid, and what advantage would require Rust model changes?
  - How should Jet handle composition, mutation/aliasing, inference/diagnostics, lifetimes/captures, cancellation/errors and measured cost?
  - How does the proposal retain one semantic mechanism and safe beginner defaults with expert control?
- **finite_peer_corpus:**
  - **item 1:**
    - **language:** Rust
    - **version:** Rust 1.98.1 (2026-09-03); commit 48a229ceaefd4985c50990b14116b6d856af0985
    - **scope:** All stable std iterator traits, methods, types, functions, producers and capability-distinct concrete relationships
    - **rationale:** Mandatory exhaustive parity baseline
  - **item 2:**

- **workloads:**
  - **item 1:**
    - **id:** gpu-w0
    - **name:** Ratified F32 vector addition
    - **definition:** F32 inputs[1,2,3] and[4,5,6], output[5,7,9]; same authored add body on selected real GPU and explicit CPU oracle; no built-in substitution
    - **reason_added:** Exact D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1=A/#3026 contract, read after initial workload selection
  - **item 2:**
    - **id:** gpu-w1
    - **name:** Integer affine map
    - **definition:** N=257 u32 values x[i]=i; y[i]=(3*x[i]+1) mod 2^32; 256 threads per group, ceil(N/256) groups; exact output y[0]=1,y[256]=769; out-of-range invocations do not access memory
  - **item 3:**
    - **id:** gpu-w2
    - **name:** Workgroup integer reduction
    - **definition:** N=256 u32 values x[i]=i; one 256-thread workgroup, shared scratch and uniform barriers; exact sum=32640; invalid conditional barrier and conflicting stores are negative cases
  - **item 4:**
    - **id:** gpu-w3
    - **name:** Compute to graphics resource handoff
    - **definition:** Compute writes a small RGBA image, graphics samples the same resource without CPU readback; explicit usages/layout/order; no game-engine expansion
  - **item 5:**
    - **id:** gpu-w4
    - **name:** AI/data tensor interop
    - **definition:** The same affine map on a contiguous u32 allocation shared with a library-owned device buffer; explicit dtype/shape/strides/device/stream ownership, no hidden host copy; no full tensor-library parity claim
  - **item 6:**
    - **id:** gpu-w5
    - **name:** F32 indexed neighbor gather
    - **definition:** F32 input[2,4,8,16,32], preserve first; average each remaining element with left neighbor; output[2,3,6,12,24]; indexed resource amendment proposed, not ratified
    - **reason_added:** Concrete required indexed/resource acceptance for #3026 without changing original W1-W4
  - **item 7:**
    - **id:** gpu-w6
    - **name:** Strict F32 workgroup reduction
    - **definition:** F32 values0..255, one256-thread group, fixed reduction order and uniform barriers, exact32640; source/profile-specific capability proof
    - **reason_added:** Strict F32 counterpart to original u32 W2; neither replaces the other
    - **rounding_control:** F32[16777216,1,-16777216],zero-padded; explicitly adjacent-pair tree expected0 vs possible reassociation1; CPU oracle same tree; proposed/not run.

  - **item 1:**

    - **id:** S-EMBED
    - **job:** An application calls user-authored rule code with structured input and receives a typed decision; separate trusted in-process native code from untrusted extensions.
  - **item 3:**
    - **id:** S-DATA
    - **job:** Read CSV/JSON, reject malformed records, aggregate ordinary values and persist/query SQLite with parameters.
  - **item 4:**
    - **id:** S-SERVICE
    - **job:** Fetch JSON over HTTP with deadlines/status checks or expose one validated service operation; include cancellation and deployment.

  - How does stock Jet compare against the finite peers with their best broadly useful libraries/tooling?

  - What are the startup/edit-run, deployment, dependency/reproducibility and native interop mechanisms?

### Shared capability rationales

- <a id="capability-rationale-001"></a> **R001** — Canonical protocol exists in source, but custom-adapter reachability and canonical method identity are not complete on the frozen paths. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-002"></a> **R002** — The public built-in Iter contract declines held next; consuming skip/first cannot preserve the same owner remainder. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-003"></a> **R003** — The captured Iter.len consumes its source. It is not nonconsuming lower/upper bounds. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-004"></a> **R004** — A consuming length route exists; exact numeric/overflow/endless behavior needs proof under Jet numeric law. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-005"></a> **R005** — Private last terminal is present. Generic ownership, failures and all-tier empty behavior remain unproved. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-006"></a> **R006** — The source has ordinary adapters, but generic demand/pull order, capability bounds and no-full-materialization are not established for every path. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-007"></a> **R007** — Short zip literal input printed2 in three frozen paths. Strict zip defaults differ intentionally; infinite, pull-order and ownership dimensions are not covered by that run. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-008"></a> **R008** — The repaired prefix proves unrequested tail is not visited in two frozen paths. Demanded failure, owned callback items and custom-source composition remain defective or unproved. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-009"></a> **R009** — The iteration mechanism exists. Effect propagation, early close and generic item ownership need exact consumers, not a helper-name match. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-010"></a> **R010** — Selection exists. Shared predicate item loans, exclusive identity, pull count and all tiers remain unproved. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-011"></a> **R011** — Rust uses Option selection. Jet filter_map deliberately keeps success and drops errors, so absence, errors-as-data and propagated failure are not interchangeable. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-012"></a> **R012** — The named Jet route deliberately replaces enumerate. Generic progression and numeric overflow behavior need evidence. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-013"></a> **R013** — A generic gate mentioning peek does not establish a held Iter lookahead protocol or restoration behavior. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-014"></a> **R014** — Stopping-sentinel consumption and source remainder are distinct from demand-limited take. Exact current contracts require focused proof. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-015"></a> **R015** — Current scan couples state and yielded clone. Independent state/output is a separate owner-gated capability. Proposed scan_emit fuses its stop; arbitrary nonfused behavior still belongs to canonical Iterator. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.
- <a id="capability-rationale-016"></a> **R016** — Captured flat_map callbacks are List-shaped. Generic Iterable children, borrowed projections and explicit Result-as-data flattening need completion. - <a id="capability-rationale-017"></a> **R017** — The ordinary Iterator contract must distinguish resumable None from permanent end. Readiness is not exhaustion. - <a id="capability-rationale-018"></a> **R018** — Exact callback schedule and reference ownership need proof; result equality alone cannot show whether callbacks ran. Proof boundary: Source contract and reviewed Jet evidence only unless exact input/executable receipt is attached; no general runtime parity claim.

### Core semantic family contracts

Each family remains a short prose block so its distinct capabilities, exports and constraints are readable without a giant repeated table cell.

#### <a id="capability-corelib-family-cpp23-libstdc-14.2-cpp-text"></a> **cpp23-libstdc++14.2:cpp-text**
- **family_id:** cpp-text
- **capabilities:** strings; string views; regular expressions; locale; character conversion; formatting and printing
- **public_exports_or_modules:** string; string_view; regex; locale; charconv; format; print; iomanip; cwchar; cwctype; cctype; cstring
- **constraints:** defaults=Not specified by the header index.; error=Error types/conditions are not enumerated by the header index; std::exception/stdexcept/system_error are separately indexed.; ownership=Declaration-level ownership and view lifetime are not captured.; allocation=Allocation behavior is not captured.; async=No async text API identified in the cited index.; platform=Hosted dialect availability; C and C++ header portability varies by implementation.; tooling=Header inclusion and dialect selection are the documented tooling surface.
- **evidence_refs:** cpp-headers-14.2
- **coverage_state:** partial
- **assessment:** The named Core owners and scoped actions below account for this family. Export presence and source contracts do not prove complete semantics, current-version parity, lifetime, allocation or execution. New gates remain unratified.

### Shared value rationales

- <a id="value-rationale-001"></a> **V001** — Reuse retired #744/c0e61zyf and #181/cauegas plus the exact EN-P01/EN-P02 receipts for the already implemented closed-choice identity/exhaustiveness baseline. Do not create another enum identity implementation card. A new current counterexample gets its own bounded repair; expanded generics, patterns and tier questions keep their separate homes.
- <a id="value-rationale-002"></a> **V002** — Create one checked-ingress investigation/proof card: identify the actual Jet public conversion path, execute valid sparse codes, holes, negative values and representation boundaries, and compare it with the captured C/C++/C#/Odin/Zig rules. Do not conflate this with C ABI layout (F15) or choose a new API silently (F20).
- <a id="value-rationale-003"></a> **V003** — Route D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1. It chooses a compiler-generated payload-free T.cases() -> Iter<T> versus explicit lists. It includes ordering, sparse-code behavior, allocation and payload rejection rules, and is explicitly a stock compiler/Core-Iter addition, not an optional enum package. General metadata is separately gated by F21.
- <a id="value-rationale-004"></a> **V004** — Reuse retired #131/c2nizvzp criteria6–8 and the narrower #2314 codec repair as existing canonical-codec work. Do not create a duplicate external/internal enum codec implementation card. Adjacent tags, unknown variants, aliases and performance remain independent choices/scopes.
- <a id="value-rationale-005"></a> **V005** — Create a matched-workload measurement card for existing Set<Enum>, explicit integer masks and dense/sparse case sets. Keep the Set public API and I1/I8 semantics fixed; any internal specialization must preserve ordering/serialization contracts. This does not authorize a new Flags/EnumSet library or a public storage switch.
- <a id="value-rationale-006"></a> **V006** — Create one recursive-tree lifecycle card: build, traverse, mutate where legal and destroy equivalent recursive/generic ASTs using Jet’s existing indirection/ownership facilities. Compare the best valid peer representations on the same tree shape and input. Flat layout and callable environments have separate cards.
- <a id="value-rationale-007"></a> **V007** — Publish the report with its worked repeated-payload and callable contrasts and durable primary citations. Do not rename enum/union or derive a speed ranking from video rhetoric or audience likes.
- <a id="value-rationale-008"></a> **V008** — Reuse retired #744/c0e61zyf criteria6 and9 for exact widening boundaries and explicit named/structural match conversions. No new bridge implementation card is justified without a fresh counterexample. F09 separately measures lowering cost.
- <a id="value-rationale-009"></a> **V009** — Create a bridge-cost card comparing direct named-enum dispatch, direct structural-union dispatch and explicit conversions on identical scalar, owned-string and view payloads.
- <a id="value-rationale-010"></a> **V010** — Create a generic-sum proof card covering concrete instantiations, nested type arguments, inference at constructors, distinct instantiations and invalid payload substitution.
- <a id="value-rationale-011"></a> **V011** — Create a focused method/trait contract card: instance and associated methods, generic methods, interface conformance, equality/copy/display derivation and existing map-key restrictions. Use ordinary shared methods or exhaustive functions for per-case behavior rather than a new case-subclass family.
- <a id="value-rationale-012"></a> **V012** — Create one inhabitation/default proof card for empty enums, singleton unit enums, singleton payload enums and empty structural unions. Locate the governing decisions, including D-AUTODERIVE1, before interpreting compiler fallback code.
- <a id="value-rationale-013"></a> **V013** — Create a pattern proof/investigation card covering nested cases, positional/named payloads, duplicate payload types, legal alternative/guard forms and mutation after narrowing. If a useful form is absent, return a specific syntax ballot rather than broadening the parser inside the proof.
- <a id="value-rationale-014"></a> **V014** — Create one diagnostic-surface card for missing cases, wrong payload arity/labels, ambiguous relative names, invalid raw codes and illegal payload-key use. Preserve what/why/fix and deterministic machine-readable repair contracts; LSP symbol operations are F33.
- <a id="value-rationale-015"></a> **V015** — Create a C ABI proof card using payload-free and legal C-layout payload enums. Test tag width, alignment, offsets, valid/invalid ingress and C-to-Jet-to-C round trips under the ratified C-layout rules.
- <a id="value-rationale-016"></a> **V016** — Create a flat-layout/locality comparison card for unit, mixed-payload and optional/error-like sums in arrays and maps. Compare the best valid C/C++/Rust/Zig/Swift/Java/C# representation for the same job, pinning versions and optimization settings.
- <a id="value-rationale-017"></a> **V017** — Create a callable-semantics card under D-CALLVALUE1, D-APILABEL1 and D-MEMPROVENANCE3: named/noncapturing/capturing values, generic call sites, argument labels, errors/effects, captured views and role-distinct wrapper types.
- <a id="value-rationale-018"></a> **V018** — Create a callable-cost card for named function items, noncapturing lambdas, small/large owned captures and escaping/non-escaping captures. Compare direct/generic/erased dispatch with equal work and the same ownership requirements.
- <a id="value-rationale-019"></a> **V019** — Route D-ENUM-EVOLUTION1: retain the closed enum law and caller-selected else (recommended), or add an explicit publisher marker requiring downstream fallback. Keep wire unknown values separate; do not reopen D-UNIONTYPE1 accidentally.
- <a id="value-rationale-020"></a> **V020** — Route D-ENUM-INGRESS1 for generated checked lookup only. Preserve Target.from_int and the ordinary fallible conversion result; never introduce from_discriminant, an optional narrowing result, or a duplicate error family.

- <a id="value-rationale-237"></a> **V237** — The source reader does not decode variants. Keep canonical tags or explicit custom codecs; do not trial-decode alternatives or infer a discriminator.
- <a id="value-rationale-238"></a> **V238** — Source delegates skipped terms to erl_interface without that local recursion bound. Proposed Core limits cover skipped input too; no source safety equivalence is asserted.
- <a id="value-rationale-239"></a> **V239** — Process, port, reference, function, cache/local/distribution identities are outside the data profile and explicitly Unsupported. No code execution or node runtime is adopted.
- <a id="value-rationale-240"></a> **V240** — The approved selected stack is serde plus serde_json. External format links establish extensibility, not selection of every crate; named formats otherwise included in this corpus remain independently accounted.
- <a id="value-rationale-241"></a> **V241** — The selected entry is core, annotations and databind. Optional modules are outside that entry, not evidence that Core lacks their features.
- <a id="value-rationale-242"></a> **V242** — These are declared non-goals. Ordinary GUI state, audio container IO and matrix interchange remain in the linked scoped work; the exclusion does not erase them.
- <a id="value-rationale-243"></a> **V243** — Keep dependency ownership in the approved application model. Account the useful service-access workflow without adding a global locator.
- <a id="value-rationale-244"></a> **V244** — Separates an independent maintenance or complete API/profile choice from the source placement ballot; neither dimension is postponed or implicitly adopted.
- <a id="value-rationale-245"></a> **V245** — Canonical protocol exists in source, but custom-adapter reachability and canonical method identity are not complete on the frozen paths.
- <a id="value-rationale-246"></a> **V246** — The public built-in Iter contract declines held next; consuming skip/first cannot preserve the same owner remainder.
- <a id="value-rationale-247"></a> **V247** — The captured Iter.len consumes its source. It is not nonconsuming lower/upper bounds.
- <a id="value-rationale-248"></a> **V248** — A consuming length route exists; exact numeric/overflow/endless behavior needs proof under Jet numeric law.
- <a id="value-rationale-249"></a> **V249** — Private last terminal is present. Generic ownership, failures and all-tier empty behavior remain unproved.
- <a id="value-rationale-250"></a> **V250** — The source has ordinary adapters, but generic demand/pull order, capability bounds and no-full-materialization are not established for every path.
- <a id="value-rationale-251"></a> **V251** — Short zip literal input printed2 in three frozen paths. Strict zip defaults differ intentionally; infinite, pull-order and ownership dimensions are not covered by that run.
- <a id="value-rationale-252"></a> **V252** — The repaired prefix proves unrequested tail is not visited in two frozen paths. Demanded failure, owned callback items and custom-source composition remain defective or unproved.
- <a id="value-rationale-253"></a> **V253** — The iteration mechanism exists. Effect propagation, early close and generic item ownership need exact consumers, not a helper-name match.
- <a id="value-rationale-254"></a> **V254** — Selection exists. Shared predicate item loans, exclusive identity, pull count and all tiers remain unproved.
- <a id="value-rationale-255"></a> **V255** — Rust uses Option selection. Jet filter_map deliberately keeps success and drops errors, so absence, errors-as-data and propagated failure are not interchangeable.
- <a id="value-rationale-256"></a> **V256** — The named Jet route deliberately replaces enumerate. Generic progression and numeric overflow behavior need evidence.
- <a id="value-rationale-257"></a> **V257** — A generic gate mentioning peek does not establish a held Iter lookahead protocol or restoration behavior.
- <a id="value-rationale-258"></a> **V258** — Stopping-sentinel consumption and source remainder are distinct from demand-limited take. Exact current contracts require focused proof.
- <a id="value-rationale-259"></a> **V259** — Current scan couples state and yielded clone. Independent state/output is a separate owner-gated capability. Proposed scan_emit fuses its stop; arbitrary nonfused behavior still belongs to canonical Iterator.
- <a id="value-rationale-260"></a> **V260** — Captured flat_map callbacks are List-shaped. Generic Iterable children, borrowed projections and explicit Result-as-data flattening need completion.
- <a id="value-rationale-261"></a> **V261** — The ordinary Iterator contract must distinguish resumable None from permanent end. Readiness is not exhaustion.
- <a id="value-rationale-262"></a> **V262** — Exact callback schedule and reference ownership need proof; result equality alone cannot show whether callbacks ran.
- <a id="value-rationale-263"></a> **V263** — Consuming an adapter currently moves Iter. A loan of the same source owner is not replay or copied output.
- <a id="value-rationale-264"></a> **V264** — Private Rust IntoIterator and List-only materialization do not establish public FromIterator-style collection relationships. Ordinary read-view stores remain semantic copies.
- <a id="value-rationale-265"></a> **V265** — Finite list outputs are not the complete Default+Extend destination relationship or typed heterogeneous partition contract.
- <a id="value-rationale-266"></a> **V266** — Failure propagation and a reusable remainder need a checked held source. A value-shaped Result carrier alone does not prove either.
- <a id="value-rationale-267"></a> **V267** — Seeded, seedless and alternate-association reductions have different empty and evaluation contracts. Generic user aggregate behavior is not established.
- <a id="value-rationale-268"></a> **V268** — The terminal family is present; empty truth values, consumed match, early failure and held remainder need exact proof.
- <a id="value-rationale-269"></a> **V269** — Materializing then reversing a List is not mixed front/back consumption of the same unconsumed range; rposition also needs exact original position accounting.
- <a id="value-rationale-270"></a> **V270** — Jet pins LAST ties, unlike Rust minimum FIRST ties. Preserve law; prove an explicit first-tie composition rather than silently redefining existing extrema.
- <a id="value-rationale-271"></a> **V271** — Current extrema callbacks are unary keys. Rust binary comparator selection is a separate missing facet; sort_by already supplies the arity convention to reuse.
- <a id="value-rationale-272"></a> **V272** — Item copying differs from copying iterator progress. Avoid duplicate aliases; prove callback ownership and noncopyable rejection.
- <a id="value-rationale-273"></a> **V273** — Current bounded cycle materializes and emits exactly n values. It cannot claim lazy infinite Clone-source replay, especially for one-shot resources.
- <a id="value-rationale-274"></a> **V274** — sum fails on each exercised frozen default/interpreter/AOT path for different reasons. Generic Sum/Product destination relationships remain unproved.
- <a id="value-rationale-275"></a> **V275** — No source-state-matched generic sequence comparison proof was supplied, including partial-order/NaN and early-consumption behavior. Do not clone method names as a second operator model.
- <a id="value-rationale-276"></a> **V276** — Sortedness, callback form and key evaluation need exact evidence. Stable Rust bool comparator differs from Ordering-returning sort callbacks.
- <a id="value-rationale-277"></a> **V277** — Canonical Item/next protocol exists; generic standard adapter dispatch and canonical identity remain incomplete.
- <a id="value-rationale-278"></a> **V278** — Iterable conversion is present, but every owned/shared/mutable relationship and adapter interoperability needs proof.
- <a id="value-rationale-279"></a> **V279** — No generic mixed front/back source contract is established; List.reverse is not equivalent.
- <a id="value-rationale-280"></a> **V280** — Consuming Iter.len does not establish nonconsuming exact remaining cardinality.
- <a id="value-rationale-281"></a> **V281** — A public behavioral capability and explicit fuse wrapper need a choice; temporary readiness must remain distinct.
- <a id="value-rationale-282"></a> **V282** — Existing materializers do not establish all generic destination relationships.
- <a id="value-rationale-283"></a> **V283** — List extension exists; a common generic destination contract is unproved.
- <a id="value-rationale-284"></a> **V284** — Numeric/helper presence does not establish the generic aggregate contract; frozen sum has tier-specific failures.
- <a id="value-rationale-285"></a> **V285** — Generic numeric, wrapper, outcome and user-aggregate product relationships need proof.
- <a id="value-rationale-286"></a> **V286** — Private factories and existing generators are reuse points, not proof of public source construction. Prove finite/once/lazy/endless and drop behavior before adding factory aliases.
- <a id="value-rationale-287"></a> **V287** — Read-only source traversal exists in source. Rust lends &T with preserved double-ended/exact/fused state; Jet default read-view storage copies and capability propagation is not proved.
- <a id="value-rationale-288"></a> **V288** — Mutable view traversal is represented in source; disjoint mutable item identities and composable held cursors remain unproved.
- <a id="value-rationale-289"></a> **V289** — Inspected Jet windows clones a rolling Vec into each output; Rust yields borrowed overlapping windows. Same values are not equivalent ownership or cost.
- <a id="value-rationale-290"></a> **V290** — Inspected Jet chunks allocates owned output groups; Rust slice chunks borrow from one owner.
- <a id="value-rationale-291"></a> **V291** — Exact/reverse chunks, retained remainder and borrowed versus disjoint mutable groups need explicit contracts; overlapping mutable windows are not presumed legal.
- <a id="value-rationale-292"></a> **V292** — Verify bytes, scalars, graphemes, Unicode expansion, invalid encoding and borrowed remainder separately; matching text names is not parity.
- <a id="value-rationale-293"></a> **V293** — Jet has a List source path, but Rust borrowed Vec iteration and its exact trait bounds are not certified.
- <a id="value-rationale-294"></a> **V294** — A mutable source path exists; Rust mutable-reference iterator identity is not established for its adapters.
- <a id="value-rationale-295"></a> **V295** — Destructive range/removal/replacement iteration has distinct mutation, partial-progress and drop semantics; current full parity is unproved.
- <a id="value-rationale-296"></a> **V296** — Jet has corresponding owned and view-shaped sources, but the three distinct move/read-borrow/write-borrow contracts must not be collapsed.
- <a id="value-rationale-297"></a> **V297** — Verify concrete source order, move/shared/exclusive item identity and capability bounds through the canonical collection/Iterable routes.
- <a id="value-rationale-298"></a> **V298** — Compare the exact set result, order, equality and ownership policy with existing Set composition; the broader selected set-operation proposal must not create a duplicate iteration mechanism.
- <a id="value-rationale-299"></a> **V299** — Prove zero/one owned/shared/mutable data iteration. Explicit Err-as-no-item selection must not erase a propagated failure.
- <a id="value-rationale-300"></a> **V300** — The inspected deferred split clones source/delimiter and emits owned String pieces. Rust str::split borrows the input; delimiter/searcher bounds and endings need separate proof.
- <a id="value-rationale-301"></a> **V301** — A range source exists; boundary arithmetic, resumption and capability propagation remain separate obligations.
- <a id="value-rationale-302"></a> **V302** — Range endpoint, step, overflow and exact-size bounds depend on concrete types; a generic range name is not a complete capability guarantee.
- <a id="value-rationale-303"></a> **V303** — An inclusive range source exists; exact/fused/double-ended bounds and endpoint overflow remain unproved.
- <a id="value-rationale-304"></a> **V304** — Verify result-item/error-effect distinction, blocking and partial resource cleanup for the named I/O source.
- <a id="value-rationale-305"></a> **V305** — Verify argument/environment encoding, ordering, snapshot behavior and the exact listed capability bounds; process strings are not automatically OS-string parity.
- <a id="value-rationale-306"></a> **V306** — Verify path components, filesystem errors and resource ownership rather than substituting ordinary text splitting.
- <a id="value-rationale-307"></a> **V307** — Blocking receive, empty-now draining and disconnection are different source contracts; keep cleanup and Pending separate from end.
- <a id="value-rationale-308"></a> **V308** — The frontend has array/collection traversal; consuming non-copy elements and preserving independent cursor capability is not certified.
- <a id="value-rationale-309"></a> **V309** — The wrapper borrows or owns iterator state; it does not change I::Item into a reference automatically. Preserve the exact capability bounds.
- <a id="value-rationale-310"></a> **V310** — The exact destination/input bounds, ownership, order, duplicate and empty/short-circuit law must be proved. A corresponding helper family is not this generic relationship.
- <a id="value-rationale-311"></a> **V311** — Canonical protocol exists; this concrete source and its Item/next bounds remain to be matched.
- <a id="value-rationale-312"></a> **V312** — The listed mixed-end capability needs one shared remaining range, not materialize-and-reverse.
- <a id="value-rationale-313"></a> **V313** — The listed exact-size bound needs a nonconsuming query; preserve specialization and overflow conditions.
- <a id="value-rationale-314"></a> **V314** — No applicable positive stable Rust row is captured for this type/capability. Table absence is not a negative impl, and does not create a Jet parity requirement.
- <a id="value-rationale-315"></a> **V315** — The listed permanent-end guarantee needs an honest capability; do not infer it for absent rows.
- <a id="value-rationale-316"></a> **V316** — Copy of cursor state and captured state needs existing ~ under exact lawful-copy bounds; no cloning of exclusive loans.
- <a id="value-rationale-317"></a> **V317** — A borrowed projection must refer to the correct remaining storage and owner; shared external storage may permit continued progress.
- <a id="value-rationale-318"></a> **V318** — Project the actual unconsumed storage with correct owner/provenance. An exclusive into_slice consumes the iterator; a view into movable owned storage restricts progress.
- <a id="value-rationale-319"></a> **V319** — Prove empty/default source construction under the listed bounds; do not add an initialization alias without a gap.
- <a id="value-rationale-320"></a> **V320** — The tail excluded from exact chunks differs from all items not yet visited.
- <a id="value-rationale-321"></a> **V321** — Exclusive remainder projection consumes the chunks iterator to prevent aliasing.
- <a id="value-rationale-322"></a> **V322** — Byte offset is distinct from scalar index and from the remaining str view.
- <a id="value-rationale-323"></a> **V323** — Range construction, endpoints/membership, or deprecated constructor behavior must use existing range/initialization semantics; do not add aliases. Exhausted inclusive-range bounds are unspecified in Rust.
- <a id="value-rationale-324"></a> **V324** — The generic Box projection returns the inner iterator I, not an item slice. Reuse the one checked Iter owner and its read-only metadata or exclusive borrowed drive; do not add a duplicate public box hierarchy.
- <a id="value-rationale-325"></a> **V325** — General Box allocation, raw-pointer, downcast or pinning machinery is not iterator functionality. Retained as evidence so it cannot inflate parity.
- <a id="value-rationale-326"></a> **V326** — The pinned Clone page explicitly forbids Clone for &mut T. Jet must likewise reject copying an exclusive borrowed source; this is not only table absence.
- <a id="value-rationale-327"></a> **V327** — One-item lookahead caches a demanded item without committing it.
- <a id="value-rationale-328"></a> **V328** — Mutable lookahead permits mutation of the retained pending item.
- <a id="value-rationale-329"></a> **V329** — Conditional consumption retains the pending item on rejection.
- <a id="value-rationale-330"></a> **V330** — Equality convenience belongs to the same conditional-read contract, not another source.
- <a id="value-rationale-331"></a> **V331** — Owned transformation must explicitly restore a returned item on Keep; a Jet error family is not this control channel.
- <a id="value-rationale-332"></a> **V332** — Borrowed transform retains permitted mutation on None; no implicit rollback.
- <a id="value-rationale-333"></a> **V333** — This index group is reconciled into the concrete entries and exact conditional bounds above; index completeness is not executed Jet parity.
- <a id="value-rationale-334"></a> **V334** — Adjacent equal-key runs need one scoped child sequence; grouping the whole input is not equivalent.
- <a id="value-rationale-335"></a> **V335** — Feed iterator input into existing grouped-query/destination machinery; preserve configured hash policy and duplicate/order behavior.
- <a id="value-rationale-336"></a> **V336** — Partition typed ordinary branches or outcomes into explicit destinations; do not turn stored errors into effects.
- <a id="value-rationale-337"></a> **V337** — Prove parser/prefix/batch/end-flush composition on held canonical sources before adding another adapter name.
- <a id="value-rationale-338"></a> **V338** — Prove exact and partial groups, fixed tuple shape and circular/replay boundaries; do not hide buffer or lifetime costs.
- <a id="value-rationale-339"></a> **V339** — Measure independently advancing consumers and bounded lookahead; an unbounded lag buffer is not a free replay capability.
- <a id="value-rationale-340"></a> **V340** — Adjacent dedup and global key history are different mechanisms. Preserve key/hash policy and do not silently retain an unbounded source.
- <a id="value-rationale-341"></a> **V341** — Specify alternate-read and end policies, including remaining one-shot inputs.
- <a id="value-rationale-342"></a> **V342** — Constant separators already belong to Jet; verify the existing operation, not a new public alias.
- <a id="value-rationale-343"></a> **V343** — A separator factory runs only between demanded values; it is not the existing repeated constant value.
- <a id="value-rationale-344"></a> **V344** — Reuse strict/short/padded zip policies; prove pull order and demanded length errors.
- <a id="value-rationale-345"></a> **V345** — Merge sorted sources with a bounded frontier and explicit comparator/tie guarantees.
- <a id="value-rationale-346"></a> **V346** — Reuse query join semantics with a sorted-source optimization only when order is proven.
- <a id="value-rationale-347"></a> **V347** — Exact grouping must preserve an incomplete remainder and distinguish reading one group from demanding the entire source fit.
- <a id="value-rationale-348"></a> **V348** — Finite positional combinations, with/without replacement and fixed/runtime width, need explicit count and ownership rules.
- <a id="value-rationale-349"></a> **V349** — Finite combinatorial enumeration must expose factorial/exponential size and ownership, not silently buffer an endless source.
- <a id="value-rationale-350"></a> **V350** — Product needs lawful replay/retained finite inputs and defined zero-dimension/order behavior; a resource cannot be reopened implicitly.
- <a id="value-rationale-351"></a> **V351** — Key evaluation, stability, cached keys and unstable sort tradeoffs need current-law proof and matched cost evidence.
- <a id="value-rationale-352"></a> **V352** — Attach to D-COLLECTION-TOPK1 and the rank-selection prototype where applicable; do not duplicate a ratified FIRST-cutoff-tie choice.
- <a id="value-rationale-353"></a> **V353** — Separate one extrema result, every tied result and extrema positions; current min_max is not all of them.
- <a id="value-rationale-354"></a> **V354** — Measure streaming text/output construction and failure behavior; a formatting view is not necessarily a prebuilt String.
- <a id="value-rationale-355"></a> **V355** — Use the canonical destination-construction/extension path instead of a second materializer family.
- <a id="value-rationale-356"></a> **V356** — Bounded tail retention and backward-aware dropping have observable demand/state costs; prove them on one-shot sources.
- <a id="value-rationale-357"></a> **V357** — Separate effects, optional selection and explicitly stored outcomes; preserve the first failure and subsequent unconsumed input.
- <a id="value-rationale-358"></a> **V358** — Prove exact search/cardinality/prefix result and partial consumption using existing primitives before adding an alias.
- <a id="value-rationale-359"></a> **V359** — Prove seedless/optional aggregate composition and empty behavior on generic types before adding duplicate names.
- <a id="value-rationale-360"></a> **V360** — Tree association is not a left fold; demonstrate order, numerical and callback-effect tradeoffs before selecting a new operator.
- <a id="value-rationale-361"></a> **V361** — Early completion is ordinary control data, not necessarily failure; preserve the source remainder.
- <a id="value-rationale-362"></a> **V362** — Reuse ordinary typed conversion and owned mapper permission; no unchecked cast channel.
- <a id="value-rationale-363"></a> **V363** — Minimum-length padding must keep an already-long source intact; it is not take or two-source zip_pad.
- <a id="value-rationale-364"></a> **V364** — Prove in-place mutable identity and short source/excess source behavior through existing view/update machinery.
- <a id="value-rationale-365"></a> **V365** — Preserve generic parallel traversal and indexed-only constraints; distinguish source-order results from callback effects, worker state, scheduling and in-flight cancellation. Reuse the existing scheduler and measured gate.
- <a id="value-rationale-366"></a> **V366** — Use the canonical Stream/effect/ownership drive; Poll/Pin/Unpin and a separate TryStream transport are foreign implementation details, not new Jet surface obligations. Exact adapter order, bounds and cleanup remain to be proved.
- <a id="value-rationale-367"></a> **V367** — Reuse existing task, source and stream ownership with the named readiness/timing/resource contract. An adapter package does not authorize adding a Tokio runtime or another public StreamExt hierarchy.
- <a id="value-rationale-368"></a> **V368** — Translate semantic capability and ownership requirements into the existing checked source/view model. Do not reproduce C++ iterator/sentinel or pipe-closure spellings as parallel Jet mechanisms.
- <a id="value-rationale-369"></a> **V369** — Keep cardinality/ordering facts honest and nonconsuming; absent exactness must not be inferred from a source class name.
- <a id="value-rationale-370"></a> **V370** — Verify the exact transform/search/control/default behavior through existing operators and canonical iteration. A captured peer name is not proof of a current Jet gap or equivalence.
- <a id="value-rationale-371"></a> **V371** — Backward/indexed traversal needs exact source capabilities and the same remaining range; a full-copy reverse is not generic parity.
- <a id="value-rationale-372"></a> **V372** — Use existing generator/Iterable/Iterator/Stream driving; preserve one-shot versus restartable source ownership and early-stop behavior.
- <a id="value-rationale-373"></a> **V373** — I/O-derived lazy sources require resource/error/demand contracts, not merely a range wrapper.
- <a id="value-rationale-374"></a> **V374** — Relational joins, textual joining and multiple-destination reduction must use their existing semantic areas rather than a new catch-all iterator library.
- <a id="value-rationale-375"></a> **V375** — Preserve owned mapper items and generic nested sources without temporary child lists or a new callback ownership dialect.
- <a id="value-rationale-376"></a> **V376** — Use the existing strict/short/padded family with explicit pull and mismatch behavior.
- <a id="value-rationale-377"></a> **V377** — Distinguish fixed/partial/strict groups, constrained batching, overlap and borrowed lifetime; reuse source/view mechanisms before naming another adapter.
- <a id="value-rationale-378"></a> **V378** — Cartesian inputs need lawful replay/finite retention and defined empty/zero-dimensional behavior.
- <a id="value-rationale-379"></a> **V379** — Preserve the distinctions among parallel splitting, bounded concurrency, ordering, in-flight work and cancellation; reuse Jet task execution rather than importing another pipeline transport.
- <a id="value-rationale-380"></a> **V380** — Use destination-owned construction and existing extension; preserve requested order, duplicates and cleanup, not a parallel collector hierarchy.
- <a id="value-rationale-381"></a> **V381** — Cross-reference the exhaustive Rust stable/candidate rows, not independent corroboration of the same upstream docs.
- <a id="value-rationale-382"></a> **V382** — Accumulator/output types, seeded/empty behavior, tie handling and association differ; prove the exact contract instead of grouping all reducers as equivalent.
- <a id="value-rationale-383"></a> **V383** — Finite positional combinatorics need explicit width/replacement/count/ownership contracts.
- <a id="value-rationale-384"></a> **V384** — Adjacent runs and global grouping/query aggregation differ in order, retention and result ownership.
- <a id="value-rationale-385"></a> **V385** — Lookahead, seekable caching and independent forks have different retention/ownership costs; no free replay claim.
- <a id="value-rationale-386"></a> **V386** — Specify alternate-read and end policy over the same source owners.
- <a id="value-rationale-387"></a> **V387** — Prove stability, tie rules, key/comparator evaluation and source-versus-callback order under existing ordering law.
- <a id="value-rationale-388"></a> **V388** — Feed existing state through the one extension protocol with explicit partial-progress semantics.
- <a id="value-rationale-389"></a> **V389** — Global membership history differs from adjacent duplicate removal; preserve key policy and retention cost.
- <a id="value-rationale-390"></a> **V390** — Verify deterministic source cleanup on break, failure, cancellation and disposal; the peer interface name does not prove current Jet cleanup.
- <a id="value-rationale-391"></a> **V391** — Typed selection, failed conversion and filtering differ. Reuse checked type tests/conversion; no unchecked runtime-cast surface is recommended.
- <a id="value-rationale-392"></a> **V392** — Lazy keyed set operations need finite membership state, representative/order rules and explicit hash/equality policy.
- <a id="value-rationale-393"></a> **V393** — Use an explicit random-state owner; current private demo-seed shuffle is not a production randomness guarantee.
- <a id="value-rationale-394"></a> **V394** — Declaration/name counts are source coverage only; the page version discrepancy and implementation limits remain explicit.
- <a id="value-rationale-395"></a> **V395** — Keep incomplete owned groups available; fixed-width extraction is not a discard-on-shortage helper.
- <a id="value-rationale-396"></a> **V396** — Return exact unadvanced remainder on end; a consuming skip is not held advancement.
- <a id="value-rationale-397"></a> **V397** — This Rust nightly name already has a Jet operation; verify existing semantics without a new alias.
- <a id="value-rationale-398"></a> **V398** — Demanded separator factory is a distinct capability from a constant separator.
- <a id="value-rationale-399"></a> **V399** — Borrowed windows require exact length and lifetime checks, not hidden per-window owned copies.

- <a id="value-rationale-403"></a> **V403** — A one-pass partition predicate is not a sorting or grouping requirement; prove composition first.

- <a id="value-rationale-408"></a> **V408** — An incomparable result differs from greater/less/equal; preserve partial-order and consumption behavior.

- <a id="value-rationale-410"></a> **V410** — Use the same checked group/view contracts, not a second iterator transport.
- <a id="value-rationale-411"></a> **V411** — Use scoped borrowed iteration; sized optimization must not force an extra public wrapper.
- <a id="value-rationale-412"></a> **V412** — Use existing generator and range mechanisms; new macro/coroutine/step names do not follow from source presence.

- <a id="value-rationale-414"></a> **V414** — Reuse the demanded-separator proposal; nightly type does not become a stable requirement.
- <a id="value-rationale-415"></a> **V415** — Do not add public unsafe TrustedLen/TrustedStep promises. Keep optimization facts in checked internal provenance; retain I9.
